question:
**The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.**

The whole family (A)/ would burst into (B)/ peals for laughter. (C)/ No Error (D)
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The primary issue in the sentence is the incorrect use of the preposition "**for**" in the phrase "peals for laughter."
 
• The correct preposition to use in this context is "**of**."
 
• "**Peals of laughter**" is a standard English idiom that means a loud, prolonged, and joyous sound of laughing.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part C** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The whole family would burst into **peals of** laughter."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "The whole family" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **B: "would burst into"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No Error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part C.
